title: refactor(payment): depend on the OTel API only, not the SDK
author: TobiTomson
body: # Changes Until now the application source depended on the OpenTelemetry SDK. That dependency is removed; the source now depends only on @opentelemetry/api. The SDK and its instrumentations are supplied by copying in the OpenTelemetry Operator's auto-instrumentation image at build time. For the payment service, this enables the use of the OTel Operator for instrumentation in Kubernetes, which is requested in #606. The same pattern can later be applied to other services as well. ## Verification: Beside the passing unit tests - which verify that generally telemetry does get generated, I verified that logs, metrics and traces generated "manually" via the OTel API also still show up. comments.author: julianocosta89
comments.text:
@TobiTomson thanks for the contribution!

One thing that I didn't understand, if the auto-instrumentation is part of the container, how does that allow SDK swap?
Shouldn't the SDK be configured to come as build arg?
If AUTO_INSTRUMENTATION==true, download the SDK and call `--require`, else skip?

comments.author: cyrille-leclerc
comments.text: Successfully tested: I see the env var `NODE_OPTIONS: --require /otel-auto-instrumentation-nodejs/autoinstrumentation.js` domnstrating I test the changed code and the trace is good: It's a great improvement 🎉

comments.author: TobiTomson
comments.text:
Good point actually - I hadn't thought of it that way. I think we need to differentiate between two things here:
1. the ability to easily swap SDKs, such as for auto-instrumentation with the operator (as requested in #606)
2. the ability to completely disable auto-instrumentation (as requested in #650)

What I've done here is 1., but it is explicitly not 2.

The way that swapping SDKs is possible is by changing the FROM in the Dockerfile that pulls it in. This approach works for docker-compose - because you can just edit the Dockerfile - and also works for the operator - because the way the operator injects the SDK is by adding an emptyDir mount to the exact same position we copied it

comments.author: julianocosta89
comments.text:
> the ability to easily swap SDKs, such as for auto-instrumentation with the operator

is that easily swappable though?

> The way that swapping SDKs is possible is by changing the FROM in the Dockerfile that pulls it in. 

If I want to use the operator, I'd need to change the Dockerfile to remove the SDK and the `--require` and later configure the operator. That is not easy.
I mean, it is easy, but how is that different from removing the SDK and rebuilding the service?

The user can do that already if they want.

Having a build arg, or an environment variable to control SDK injected `true/false`, and even point to the SDK would be easier, because then the user do not need to rebu

comments.author: TobiTomson
comments.text: To use the operator you don't need to change anything. You use this image, and it just works (because it is now able to just swap out what we baked into the image at runtime). Which was not the case before. That's exactly why I did this change.
